checks.fix: A short that runs long is usually two moments in one; keep the one that lands and drop the other.
A vertical clip is watched without sound first. Turn the captions on.
The caption line is cut in half by the seam of the split. Move the band below it.
The captions sit over the camera half; they read better on the screen half.
Nothing says what the clip is about. Write a hook of a few words, or pick a clip that opens on its own question.
A hook longer than a line is a sentence, and it is read after the clip has already been scrolled past.
A pause this long in a short is dead air. Cut it, unless it is the beat before a punchline.
What is on the screen is the content; a picture over it covers the thing being talked about.

rubric.ask: If the clip answers somebody, does it open on their message, with the hook coming in as it goes? If nobody asked, does it open on the hook rather than on an invented comment?
rubric.fix: Extend the head to the message, or drop the comment and open on the hook.

rubric.ask: Does the clip make sense to somebody who has never watched the stream — no missing question, no reference to something said before it starts?
rubric.fix: Move the start back to where the thing being answered is stated, or pick a moment that carries its own context.

rubric.ask: Does the clip end after the point lands, with the reaction to it if there is one, rather than before it or long after?
rubric.fix: Move the end to just after the last word of the payoff.

rubric.ask: Does the first word start a sentence rather than continue one?
rubric.fix: Move the start to the beginning of the sentence; a clip that opens mid-phrase reads as a mistake.
